## Load packages

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(cowplot)
library(ComplexUpset)

theme_set(theme_cowplot())
```

## Read and load data

```{r}
FF_genomes_raw <- read.table('../../../Big_data/FlyingFlies_SNPtable.txt', header = T)

# Note: frequency here refers to Reference allele frequency. If freq is low, then alternate allele frequency is high. 
# This is based on the PERL code where:
# (line 56) my $TotalCount = $A + $B;
# (line 61) my $RefFreq = $A/$TotalCount

# N refers to total coverage:
# (line 62) $temp = $temp."\t".sprintf("%.2f",$RefFreq)."\t$TotalCount";

```

## Data cleanup and apply filters

### Create filters for allele frequency and read depth

Allele frequency: #REF suggests a filter of \>3 alleles. This is calculated and filtered.

Ferretti et al 2013 suggest removing all singleton reads.

Read depth: Ferretti et al 2013 suggest that a read depth of 20-30 is a good minimum, and statistical power does not increase beyond a read depth of 40-50. Burke et al. used an upper cutoff of 150.

As of 2026-05-15, read depth filters of min. 20× and max. 150× will be applied.

Gamboa-Santarosa et al 2026 bioRxiv have filtered read depth between 50-500. For allele frequency, they have filtered a combined allele frequency of 1% on both ends.

2026-05-20: Read depth filters of min. 20x and max. 500x. Allele frequency (averaged over all samples) of \<0.01 and \>0.99 are filtered.

2026-06-02: After further discussions, it is determined that the filter policy will be:

read depth: min. 20x, max. 500x (unchanged from previous implementation).

allele frequency: ALL alleles at a site should be \>0.01 and \<0.99. Furthermore, all sites containing a singleton count will be removed.

2026-06-08: the filtering out of a SNP for ANY allele being less than 0.01 or 0.99 was thought to be too conservative. With read depth as well, the filter will be changed to ensuring that the max. value of a SNP should not be less than 20 and the min. value of a SNP should not be more than 500. Singleton filtering removed, since one singleton at a site out of 8 populations is too conservative. The allele frequency filtering should account for improbably low reads. As an addition, the sites which are found significantly differentiated based on the linear model analysis will be checked post analysis for the allele frequency and read depth distributions.

```{r}
# Remove all garbled chromosome names, as well as the 4th and Y chromosome. Set CHROM as factor for easier plotting later. Even though chromosome names have been filtered, the 'unfiltered' in the variable name here refers strictly to allele frequency and read depth. 
# Remove all NAs. 
FF_genomes_unfiltered <- FF_genomes_raw %>% filter(CHROM %in% c("2L", "2R", "3L", "3R", "X")) %>% mutate_at("CHROM", as.factor) %>% drop_na()

prefilter_length <- length(FF_genomes_unfiltered$POS)

# Convert data to long form for easier filtering and diagnostics. Change N_ to depth.
FF_genomes_unfiltered <-  FF_genomes_unfiltered %>% 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(starts_with("freq_"), starts_with("N_")),
    names_to = c(".value", "Population"),
    names_pattern = "(freq_|N_)(.*)"
  ) %>% rename(depth_ = N_) %>% 
  mutate(ref_count = round(freq_ * depth_)) %>% 
  # Removes all text after the second underscore,
  # used to remove _G13_sample...
  # this leaves freq_CON1, N_CON1, and so on.
  mutate(Population = str_remove(Population, "_.*"))

# filtering out criteria: 
# all singletons
# read depth min 20x, max 500x
# ref freq max > 0.01 and min < 0.99
min_depth <- 20
max_depth <- 500
min_freq <- 0.01
max_freq <- 0.99

# Pre-filter diagnostics
FF_filter_summary <- FF_genomes_unfiltered %>% 
  summarise(
    total_snps = n(),
    na_freq = sum(is.na(freq_)),
    na_depth = sum(is.na(depth_)),
    fail_singleton = sum(ref_count == 1 | ref_count == (depth_ - 1)),
    fail_mindepth = sum(depth_ < min_depth),
    fail_maxdepth = sum(depth_ > max_depth),
    fail_minfreq = sum(freq_ < min_freq),
    fail_maxfreq = sum(freq_ > max_freq),
    # Ensures that Nmiss has no value >0
    Nmiss_check = sum(Nmiss),
    .by = Population
  )

# apply filters and convert to wide format for easier analyses. drop Nmiss.
FF_genomes_filtered <-  FF_genomes_unfiltered %>% 
  select(-Nmiss) %>% 
  group_by(CHROM, POS) %>% 
  filter(!any(
    # singleton filter
    ref_count==1 | ref_count==(depth_-1) |
    # read depth filter
    depth_ < min_depth | depth_ > max_depth |
    # allele frequency filter
    freq_ < min_freq | freq_ > max_freq
    )) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  select(-ref_count) %>% 
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Population,
    values_from = c(freq_, depth_),
    names_glue = "{.value}{Population}"
  )

filtered_out <- prefilter_length - length(FF_genomes_filtered$POS)

```

#### Save filtered data

```{r}
saveRDS(FF_genomes_filtered,
        file = "../../../Big_data/FF_genomes_filtered.RDS")
```

#### Make summary plots for SNP count across chromosomes, read depth and allele frequency distributions, filtered numbers

```{r}
# Make a plot of count of chromosomes using raw data
plot_chrom_counts <- FF_genomes_raw %>% 
  mutate(Chromosome =
  fct_other(
    CHROM, c("X", "Y", "2L", "2R", "3L", "3R", "4"), other_level = "Others")
  ) %>% 
  count(Chromosome) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = Chromosome, y = log10(n))) +
geom_col(fill = "lightblue", color = "darkblue")+
  geom_text(aes(label=n), 
            vjust=2, color = 'red', fontface = 'bold',
            size = 4) +
  labs(title = "Counts of SNPs at each Chromosome",
         x = "Chromosome",
         y = "log10(SNP count)")
  
print(plot_chrom_counts)

# Process data for read depth and allele frequency plots
FF_filter_status <- FF_genomes_unfiltered %>% 
  group_by(CHROM, POS) %>% 
  mutate(depth_filter = ifelse(depth_ < min_depth |depth_ > max_depth,
                               "remove", "retain"),
         freq_filter = ifelse(freq_ < min_freq | freq_ > max_freq,
                               "remove", "retain"),
         single_filter = ifelse(ref_count == 1 | ref_count == (depth_ - 1),
                               "remove", "retain")
         )

# Depth filter plot: does not account for positional filtering. i.e., one position may have multiple reads above 20x but still gets filtered. This histogram will be confusing if colored by removed depth at a given position, since one of those may be below 20x but ALL at the position will be filtered out. Same logic holds for allele frequency plot. Both are commented out for this reason, and instead the Venn diagram is shown.

rdepth_plot <- ggplot(data = FF_filter_status,
          aes(x = log10(depth_), fill = depth_filter, color = depth_filter)) +
  geom_histogram(
    aes(y = after_stat(log10(count + 1))),
    binwidth = 0.05, position = "identity", alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("retain" = 'steelblue2', "remove" = 'salmon'))+
  scale_color_manual(values = c("retain" = 'darkblue', "remove" = 'darkred'))+

  geom_vline(xintercept = c(log10(min_depth), log10(max_depth)),
             color = 'darkred', linetype = 'dashed') +
  labs(title = "Read depth histogram\nfiltered at min. 20 and max. 500",
       x = "log10(read depth)",
       y = "log10(count + 1)")

print(rdepth_plot)

# Allele frequency filter plot
freq_plot <- ggplot(data = FF_filter_status,
          aes(x = freq_, fill = freq_filter, color = freq_filter)) +
  geom_histogram(
    aes(y = after_stat(log10(count + 1))),
    binwidth = 0.01, position = "identity", alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("retain" = 'cyan', "remove" = 'salmon'))+
  scale_color_manual(values = c("retain" = 'cyan4', "remove" = 'darkred'))+

  geom_vline(xintercept = c(min_freq, max_freq),
             color = 'darkred', linetype = 'dashed') +
  labs(title = "Ref. frequency histogram\nfiltered at min. 0.01 and max. 0.99",
       x = "ref. allele frequency",
       y = "log10(count + 1)")

print(freq_plot)

#                labs(title = "Total Filtered")

```
